title: Pass every time
eyebrow: CETI · agent reliability, one try versus every try
lede: A board of 460 tries, lit 60 % of the time, is stood up, re-sorted by passes and cut by 'every try': only 44 of 115 tasks pass all four.
captions: An agent that is usually right does most of the work.
Or does it? Count every try, task by task.
A customer-service test: GPT-4o on tau-bench retail.
115 tasks. One tile each.
Four tries per task. One cube per try.
That is 460 cubes.
Light every cube that passed.
278 passed. A lit cube is a pass.
Tries that pass: 60.4 %.
Stand the board up. Each task becomes a column.
Four tries stacked. Some lit all the way, some not.
Judge a task by all its tries, not by one.
Sort the columns by how many tries passed.
44 tasks pass all four tries.
22 never pass.
Same tasks, new question: pass every try, not one.
Two tries, both pass: 49.1 %.
Three tries, all pass: 43.0 %.
Four tries: 44 of 115 tasks pass them all.
All four tries pass: 38.3 %.
The paper's own run at eight tries: under 25 %.
A one-try score hides what every try shows.
Passing a benchmark is not the same as shipping.
296 PRs pass the tests.
Top SWE-bench Verified score: 80.9 %.
4 maintainers read them. Would they merge?
About half would not be merged.
One more yardstick: how long a task can it do?
27 minutes at the 80 % bar.
Another agent, same idea: one cube per minute.
4 h 49 min at the 50 % bar.
About 10 times longer.
On Monday, ask for the every-time number.

brand.takeaway: A pass is not a pass every time.

sources: tau-bench README leaderboard, retail, TC (gpt-4o): Pass^1..4 = 0.604 / 0.491 / 0.430 / 0.383 (opened and read 2026-10-10) ; model GPT-4o, 2024 — https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench

tau-bench historical_trajectories/gpt-4o-retail.json: 460 rows = 115 tasks x 4 trials, per-task reward 0/1; tasks_test.py has 115 retail tasks (downloaded and recomputed 2026-10-10) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sierra-research/tau-bench/main/historical_trajectories/gpt-4o-retail.json

Yao, Shinn, Razavi, Narasimhan 2024, tau-bench, abstract: about 61 % pass^1 on retail, 'as low as ~25 % for pass^8'; paper PDF blocked by egress (403), abstract seen as quoted in search results — https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045

METR note 2026-03-10: 4 active maintainers, 3 SWE-bench Verified repos, 296 AI PRs, roughly half of test-passing PRs would not be merged; agents could not iterate on feedback (METR page blocked by egress; read through search-result text of the note and four outlets quoting it) — https://metr.org/notes/2026-03-10-many-swe-bench-passing-prs-would-not-be-merged-into-main/

METR time-horizon measurement for Claude Opus 4.5: 50 % horizon about 4 h 49 min (95 % CI 1 h 49 min to 20 h 25 min), 80 % horizon 27 min — https://x.com/metr_evals (Dec 2025 post; reported by https://www.techmeme.com/251221/p1 and https://the-decoder.com/anthropics-claude-opus-4-5-can-tackle-some-tasks-lasting-nearly-five-hours/)

Anthropic, Claude Opus 4.5 announcement 2025-11-24: 80.9 % on SWE-bench Verified (vendor-reported; read through secondary coverage, announcement page not opened) — https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5
recompute.py: beta model of the published curve, mulberry32 seed 20261010 (simulation claim) — factory/topics/pass-every-time/recompute.py
honest: One 2024 model, and agents that could not revise: newer ones may do better.
